principle.name: Respect the artifact‑based workflow
principle.description: The public behavior of the compiler is defined by the checked artifacts under `artifacts/omega/`. Changes to the self‑hosted source must be validated against those artifacts before claiming support.
principle.rationale: Keeps documentation and user expectations aligned with what the released compiler actually does.

example.good: Verify that the optimization is enabled in the checked JIT or GPU artifact
example.bad: Assume the optimization is available because the source code exists

principle.name: Maintain single source of truth
principle.description: Compiler invariants and semantics should be defined in one place (usually the checker). Avoid duplicating logic across frontend, IR, and backends.
principle.rationale: Reduces drift and makes the compiler easier to reason about.

example.good: Add the rule in `self‑hosted/check/` and let lowering propagate it
example.bad: Re‑implement the same rule in each backend separately

principle.name: Prefer localized edits
principle.description: When fixing a bug or adding a feature, modify the smallest set of files necessary. Avoid large‑scale refactoring unless it is explicitly requested.
principle.rationale: Keeps changes reviewable and reduces risk of introducing regressions.

example.scenario: Fixing a parser error recovery issue
example.good: Edit only the relevant recovery functions in `self‑hosted/parser/`
example.bad: Rewrite the entire parser state machine

convention.rule: Use snake_case for functions and variables, PascalCase for types
Keep functions short and focused; split large functions into helpers

pitfall.description: Assuming a backend feature is globally enabled
pitfall.why_problematic: The checked JIT artifact may have GPU codegen disabled, while the separate GPU artifact has it enabled. Claims about GPU support must be qualified by which artifact is being discussed.
pitfall.correct_approach: Always check the artifact capabilities via `souc info` and refer to the appropriate artifact profile in documentation.

pitfall.description: Forgetting to update the relevant test suite
pitfall.why_problematic: Compiler changes that affect diagnostics or runtime behavior can break existing tests. Without updating the tests, the CI will fail.
pitfall.correct_approach: After any change, run the corresponding test suite (run‑pass, compile‑fail, stdlib) and adjust expectations if necessary.

category.name: before_starting
category.item: Understand which compiler subsystem is affected
Locate the existing tests for that subsystem

category.name: during_implementation
category.item: Follow the existing code style and naming conventions
Add inline comments for non‑obvious logic
Keep related changes together in a single commit

category.name: before_completion
category.item: Run the full test suite for the affected area
Verify the change works with both JIT and GPU artifacts if applicable
Update any documentation that mentions the changed behavior
